title: Finite free etale chart with a power-containing ideal lift
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Fix a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset B$, an element $a\in A$, an integer $m\ge1$, and a finite list $j_1,\ldots,j_r\in B$ generating an ideal $J\subset B$ such that $a_B^m\in J$, where $a_B$ is the image of $a$. There exist $g\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$, a monic polynomial $f\in A[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], an element $h\in C=A[T]/(f)$, and an $A$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:B_g\xrightarrow{\sim}C_h$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] with the following properties. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C_h\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale, and $C$ has $A$-basis $1,t,\ldots,t^{d-1}$, where $d=\deg f\ge0$ and $t$ is the class of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. There are $c_i\in C$ and integers $e_i\ge0$ with $\theta(j_i/1)=c_i/h^{e_i}$ for $1\le i\le r$. Writing $a_C$ for the image of $a$, the ideal $K=(c_1,\ldots,c_r,a_C^m)\subset C$ is finitely generated and satisfies $KC_h=\theta(JB_g)$ and $a_C^m(C/K)=0$. Here each extended ideal is generated by its images, and $\theta(JB_g)$ denotes the image ideal under $\theta$.

source.place: Tag 0813, lemma-push-ideal, proof: standard-etale monic quotient chart and numerator generators h_1,...,h_n with h_(n+1)=a^m (old item steps 2-3).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-locally-standard] to the given etale map and prime $\mathfrak q$. Obtain $g\notin\mathfrak q$, a monic $f\in A[T]$, a polynomial $H\in A[T]$, and an $A$-algebra isomorphism $B_g\cong A[T][Y]/(f,YH-1)$. Its hypotheses are exactly the etaleness and primality assumed here.

Put $C=A[T]/(f)$ and let $h$ be the class of $H$. Identify $A[T][Y]/(f,YH-1)$ with $C_h$: send $T$ to $t/1$ and $Y$ to $1/h$, and in the opposite direction send $[P]/h^e$ to $P(T)Y^e$. The relations $f=0$ and $YH=1$ make these well-defined, and their composites fix the ring generators and every fraction. Composing with Step 1 gives the required $A$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:B_g\cong C_h$.

source.place: Tag 0813, lemma-push-ideal, proof: standard-etale monic quotient chart and numerator generators with the prescribed power adjoined.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}B_g$ is the open subscheme $D(g)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Apply [lem-a1-etale-open-restriction] to the given etale morphism, with source open $D(g)$ and whole target $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}B_g\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale. The $A$-algebra isomorphism $\theta$ identifies this morphism with $\operatorname{Spec}C_h\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, proving its etaleness.

source.place: Tag 02GJ, lemma-etale-characterize, restriction to compatible opens; schemes.tex Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] to the monic $f$ of Step 1. It gives the asserted $A$-basis $1,t,\ldots,t^{d-1}$ of $C$, for $d=\deg f$. The prime $\mathfrak q$ forces $B\ne0$ and hence $A\ne0$, so the degree of the monic polynomial is an ordinary nonnegative integer.

source.place: Tag 0813, lemma-push-ideal, proof: standard-etale monic quotient chart and numerator generators with the prescribed power adjoined.

proof.text: For each $i$, write $x_i=\theta(j_i/1)$. The fraction description in [def-weil-ring-localization-away] supplies $c_i\in C$ and $e_i\ge0$ with $x_i=c_i/h^{e_i}$. This is a finite list of choices; for $r=0$ it is empty. Define $K=(c_1,\ldots,c_r,a_C^m)$, a finitely generated ideal by its displayed finite generating list.

source.place: Tag 0813, lemma-push-ideal, proof: standard-etale monic quotient chart and numerator generators with the prescribed power adjoined.

proof.text: Write $L=\theta(JB_g)=(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\subset C_h$. Since $c_i/1=h^{e_i}x_i$ and $x_i=(1/h^{e_i})(c_i/1)$, the ideals generated by the $x_i$ and by the $c_i/1$ coincide. Choose $b_i\in B$ with $a_B^m=\sum_i b_i j_i$, using $a_B^m\in J$. Applying $\theta$ after localization gives $a_C^m/1=\sum_i\theta(b_i/1)x_i\in L$, because $\theta$ is an $A$-algebra map. Thus adjoining $a_C^m/1$ adds nothing and $KC_h=L$. Finally $a_C^m[z]=[a_C^mz]=0$ in $C/K$ for every $z\in C$, since $a_C^m\in K$. This proves the annihilation clause, also when $r=0$ or $K=C$.
